message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"7.6","text":"As Peter entered Sidon, people carried many in on beds and laid them before him. But he said to them, “Then do not suppose that I can do anything for your healing, since I am myself a mortal man capable of falling prey to many sufferings. But I do not begrudge showing you the way by which you will be able to be saved, for I myself learned from the prophet of truth the determinations of God, foreordained ‘before the foundation of the world.’ I mean the evil actions for which he appointed human beings to be afflicted by the ruler of wickedness, and likewise the good actions for which he determined that those who first believed in him as he healed the bodies would be saved, and afterward that their souls too would be restored to imperishability.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Μὴ τοίνυν νομίσητε ἐμέ τι δύνασθαι πρὸς ὑμετέραν ἴασιν","chosen":"Then do not suppose that I can do anything for your healing","rationale":"The infinitive construction expresses what the hearers must not suppose; πρὸς ὑμετέραν ἴασιν indicates ability directed toward their healing."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς προωρισμένους τοῦ θεοῦ „πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου“ ὁρισμούς","chosen":"the determinations of God, foreordained ‘before the foundation of the world’","rationale":"“Foreordained determinations” preserves the source’s repetition of the ὁρίζω word group rather than replacing it with unrelated English terms."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ ποίαις κακαῖς πράξεσιν","chosen":"the evil actions for which","rationale":"Here ἐπί with the dative introduces the actions or conditions on account of which the stated consequence was appointed."},{"source_quote":"πρότερον πιστεύσαντας αὐτῷ ἰωμένῳ τὰ σώματα","chosen":"those who first believed in him as he healed the bodies","rationale":"πρότερον is taken with πιστεύσαντας, in contrast with the following ἔπειτα. The dative αὐτῷ ἰωμένῳ can also be understood as “believed him, the one healing the bodies,” and the precise referent of “him” remains contextually ambiguous."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ ἀνώλεθρον","chosen":"to imperishability","rationale":"The substantivized adjective denotes the imperishable or indestructible state toward which the souls are restored."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"7.7","text":"Knowing, then, both these good and evil actions, I announce them to you beforehand as two roads, showing you along which one people perish as they walk and along which one they are saved as they travel, guided by God. The road of those who perish is broad and very smooth, but it brings destruction without toil; the road of those who are saved is narrow and rough, but at the end it saves those who have traversed it laboriously. At the head of these two roads sit unbelief and faith. Those who have preferred pleasures travel by way of unbelief; because of those pleasures . . . . they did not even continue to seek what is beneficial. Yet they do not know that God’s purposes are not like human purposes. For first of all, he knows everyone’s thoughts, and each person is held accountable not only for undertaking something but also for intending it. Those who try to think what is good and fail act far less impiously than those who do not attempt good things at all. For God himself saw fit that the person who lapses despite knowing what is good should, after being punished moderately in proportion to human transgressions, be saved. But those who have neglected even to begin to know what is better—even if they do countless other good things—but do not adopt the religious observance he himself prescribed will, having incurred a charge of negligence, be utterly extinguished by the greatest punishment.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προκαθέζεται ἀπιστία καὶ πίστις","chosen":"At the head of these two roads sit unbelief and faith","rationale":"προκάθημαι depicts unbelief and faith as positioned before or at the head of their respective roads."},{"source_quote":"οὐδὲ ζητεῖν τὸ συμφέρον οὐ διεφύλαξαν","chosen":"they did not even continue to seek what is beneficial","rationale":"διαφυλάσσω with the infinitive is understood as maintaining or continuing an activity. The two negatives are treated as emphatic negative concord; a strictly logical double-negative reading is possible in isolation but is contextually less likely, and the preceding printed gap prevents certainty."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἐν τῷ ἐνχειρῆσαι μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ ἐννοῆσαι","chosen":"not only for undertaking something but also for intending it","rationale":"The contrast extends accountability from beginning an action to conceiving or intending it; “something” and “it” represent the implicit object shared by the two infinitives."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ἐγχειροῦντες καλὰ νοεῖν καὶ ἀποτυγχάνοντες","chosen":"Those who try to think what is good and fail","rationale":"The rendering preserves νοεῖν as mental activity rather than adding an action not explicitly stated."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ λόγον τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων παραπτωμάτων μετρίως κολασθέντα","chosen":"after being punished moderately in proportion to human transgressions","rationale":"κατὰ λόγον is attached to the punishment and expresses proportion. It could instead qualify the manner of the person’s lapse, but its proximity to κολασθέντα supports the chosen attachment."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ᾗ δὲ αὐτὸς ὥρισεν θρησκείᾳ μὴ γένωνται","chosen":"but do not adopt the religious observance he himself prescribed","rationale":"Literally, they do not “come to be in” the θρησκεία he determined. “Adopt the religious observance” gives that idiom intelligible English without reducing θρησκεία merely to inward belief."},{"source_quote":"ἀποσβεσθήσονται","chosen":"will be utterly extinguished","rationale":"The verb uses the image of quenching or extinguishing, which is retained rather than generalized to “will be punished” or “will perish.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"δι’ ἃς . . . . οὐδὲ ζητεῖν τὸ συμφέρον οὐ διεφύλαξαν","issue":"The four-dot printed gap marks unavailable or omitted wording within the causal statement. It interrupts the syntax and prevents recovery of the clause’s complete content; no restoration has been supplied.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἄνευ του πόνου","issue":"The article is printed as του without the expected circumflex. This is an accentual feature and does not affect the meaning.","proposed_reading":"ἄνευ τοῦ πόνου","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐνχειρῆσαι","issue":"The print has the orthographic form ἐνχειρῆσαι where the assimilated compound spelling ἐγχειρῆσαι is more usual. The form remains intelligible as the aorist infinitive of “undertake.”","proposed_reading":"ἐγχειρῆσαι","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7.8","text":"The religious observance appointed by him is this: to worship him alone; to believe the one prophet of truth; to be baptized “for forgiveness of sins” and thus, through the purest immersion, to be born anew to God through the water that saves; not to partake of “a table of demons” (I mean things sacrificed to idols, animals found dead, strangled animals, animals caught by wild beasts, and blood); not to live in impurity; to bathe after intercourse with a woman, while women themselves must also observe menstrual separation; for everyone to practice self-control, do good, and not act unjustly; and to await eternal life from the all-powerful God, asking through continual prayers and petitions to receive it. As Peter gave such exhortations in Sidon, within a few days many there too reoriented themselves, believed, and were healed. He established a church, appointed one of the elders accompanying him as their overseer, and departed from Sidon.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας μόνῳ πιστεύειν προφήτῃ","chosen":"to believe the one prophet of truth","rationale":"μόνῳ characterizes the prophet as the sole or one prophet of truth. The phrase could also be rendered “to believe only the prophet of truth,” with the exclusivity attached adverbially to believing."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τῆς ἁγνοτάτης βαφῆς","chosen":"through the purest immersion","rationale":"βαφή denotes dipping or immersion and here refers to the preceding baptism; the superlative force of ἁγνοτάτης is retained."},{"source_quote":"ἀναγεννηθῆναι θεῷ διὰ τοῦ σώζοντος ὕδατος","chosen":"to be born anew to God through the water that saves","rationale":"The rendering preserves both the God-directed dative θεῷ and the source’s direct description of the water as saving."},{"source_quote":"νεκρῶν, πνικτῶν, θηριαλώτων","chosen":"animals found dead, strangled animals, animals caught by wild beasts","rationale":"These substantivized plurals occur in a list of prohibited foods. “Animals found dead” expresses νεκρῶν contextually; more literally it is simply “dead things.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀπὸ κοίτης γυναικὸς λούεσθαι","chosen":"to bathe after intercourse with a woman","rationale":"κοίτη γυναικός literally refers to a woman’s bed but in this purity context denotes sexual intercourse."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὰς μέντοι καὶ ἄφεδρον φυλάσσειν","chosen":"while women themselves must also observe menstrual separation","rationale":"ἄφεδρος is a term for menstruation or the associated period of separation. The phrase may also be rendered “observe the menstrual period”; the source does not explicitly repeat the preceding command to bathe."},{"source_quote":"μετανοησάντων","chosen":"reoriented themselves","rationale":"The context describes moral and religious redirection accompanying belief; the traditional alternative is “repented.” No Godward phrase is added because the Greek does not state one here."},{"source_quote":"ἐπίσκοπον","chosen":"overseer","rationale":"The word designates the supervisory office assigned to the elder; “bishop” is a possible institutional rendering but may imply a later fixed title."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"7.9","text":"As soon as he set foot in Berytus, an earthquake occurred. The crowds approached Peter and said, “Help us! For we are afraid,” they declared, “that perhaps we may all be utterly destroyed.” Then Simon, taking courage, together with Appion, Anubion, Athenodorus, and the rest of his companions, publicly shouted to the crowds against Peter: “Flee from this man, men! He is a magician—believe it! He himself brought the earthquake upon us and stirred up the diseases, so that he might overawe you as though he himself were a god.” Simon’s party made many such false claims against Peter, alleging that he possessed power beyond human capacity. But when the crowds fell silent for him, Peter gave a slight smile and said with startling boldness, “Men, I acknowledge that, if God wills, I am able to do the very things these men say. What is more, if you do not heed me in what I say, I am ready to tear your entire city up from its foundations.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπέβη τῆς Βηρυτοῦ","chosen":"set foot in Berytus","rationale":"ἐπιβαίνω with the genitive can denote entering or setting foot in a place; “Berytus” preserves the ancient city name rather than modernizing it to Beirut."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὸν σεισμὸν αὐτὸς ἐποίησεν ἡμῖν","chosen":"He himself brought the earthquake upon us","rationale":"The dative ἡμῖν presents the earthquake as something caused for or against the speakers; “upon us” conveys the hostile result."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα ὑμᾶς καταπλήξεται","chosen":"so that he might overawe you","rationale":"καταπλήσσω can denote terrifying, stunning, or overwhelming with amazement. “Overawe” fits the accusation that Peter is using wonders to induce a false perception of divinity."},{"source_quote":"ὡς αὐτὸς ὢν θεός","chosen":"as though he himself were a god","rationale":"The anarthrous predicate θεός permits “a god,” while “God” is also possible in the work’s monotheistic setting. The chosen wording preserves the accusers’ comparison without identifying Peter with the supreme God unambiguously."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ὑπὲρ δύναμιν ἀνθρωπίνην δυναμένου τοῦ Πέτρου","chosen":"alleging that he possessed power beyond human capacity","rationale":"The ὡς construction presents this superhuman ability as the content or guise of Simon’s party’s false allegations."},{"source_quote":"καταπληκτικῇ τῇ παρρησίᾳ","chosen":"with startling boldness","rationale":"παρρησία denotes open, confident speech, while καταπληκτική marks its astonishing or overwhelming effect."},{"source_quote":"τὴν πᾶσαν ὑμῶν ἐκβαθρεῦσαι πόλιν","chosen":"to tear your entire city up from its foundations","rationale":"ἐκβαθρεύω evokes uprooting or razing down to the foundations, an image stronger than simply “destroy.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα ὑμᾶς καταπλήξεται","issue":"The purpose clause is printed with the future indicative καταπλήξεται after ἵνα rather than the more classically expected subjunctive. Such use is defensible as later Greek syntax, and the supplied reading clearly supports a purpose clause without emendation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7.10","text":"When the crowds became frightened and promised to act otherwise as they might be commanded by him, Peter said, “None of you is to associate with these sorcerers or mingle with them.” As soon as the crowds heard the brief command, they picked up sticks and pursued them until they had driven them completely out of the city. Then the sick and demon-possessed among them came in and threw themselves at Peter’s feet. But when he saw this and wished to dispel their consternation, he said to them:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἑτέρως ποιήσειν ἐπαγγειλαμένων ὅπερ ἂν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ κελεύωνται","chosen":"promised to act otherwise as they might be commanded by him","rationale":"The supplied ἑτέρως is taken in its normal sense, “differently” or “otherwise,” indicating a promised change of conduct in accordance with Peter’s commands."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς γόησιν","chosen":"with these sorcerers","rationale":"γόης can denote a sorcerer, charlatan, or impostor. “Sorcerers” fits the immediately preceding accusation of magic, though “charlatans” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κελεύσματος τοῦ συντόμου","chosen":"the brief command","rationale":"σύντομος characterizes the command as concise or terse; “brief” preserves its form without adding an emotional tone."},{"source_quote":"ξύλα λαβόντες","chosen":"they picked up sticks","rationale":"ξύλα literally denotes pieces of wood; in the pursuit scene, “sticks” expresses their likely use without specifying weapons more precisely than the source."},{"source_quote":"οἱ νοσοῦντες αὐτῶν καὶ δαιμονῶντες","chosen":"the sick and demon-possessed among them","rationale":"αὐτῶν most naturally refers to the crowds, though grammatically it could be heard as a possessive “their.” “Among them” avoids implying that the crowds owned or controlled the afflicted people."},{"source_quote":"τὴν κατάπληξιν αὐτῶν ἀναλῦσαι","chosen":"to dispel their consternation","rationale":"κατάπληξις can be amazement, shock, or terror. In the aftermath of Peter’s threat and the people’s prostration, “consternation” preserves both alarm and astonishment."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἑτέρως ποιήσειν ἐπαγγειλαμένων ὅπερ ἂν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ κελεύωνται","issue":"The adverb ἑτέρως (“differently”) produces a compressed connection with the following relative clause, but it can defensibly mean that the crowds promised to change their conduct in conformity with his commands. The smoother ἑτοίμως (“readily”) is a possible conjecture only and has not been used in the translation.","proposed_reading":"ἑτοίμως ποιήσειν ἐπαγγειλαμένων ὅπερ ἂν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ κελεύωνται","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
